'''''Nymphaea mexicana''''' is a species of [[aquatic plant]] that is native to the [[Southern United States]] and [[Mexico]] as far south as [[Michoacán]].<ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN | accessdate=2010-04-19}}</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Nymphaea%20mexicana.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref> Common names include '''yellow water lily''', '''Mexican water lily''' and '''banana water lily'''.

==Description==
[[File:Nymphaea mexicana Zucc. stolon.jpg|upright|thumb|''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zucc. stolon with scale bar (3 cm) on a white background]]
[[File:Nymphaea Mexicana Blatt.jpg|thumb|right|Upper leaf surface]]
[[File:Nymphaea mexicana Zucc. (AM AK298722-3).jpg|thumb|right|Longitudinally cut rhizome]]
[[File:Nymphaea mexicana (27) 1200.jpg|right|thumb|A close-up of the flower]]

===Vegetative characteristics===
''Nymphaea mexicana'' is a rhizomatous,<ref name = "Flora of North America">''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zuccarini. (n.d.). Flora of North America @ efloras.org. Retrieved December 2, 2024, from http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=233500827</ref> aquatic,<ref name = "Biota of New Zealand" /> perennial herb<ref name = "Calflora">The Calflora Database. (n.d.). ''Nymphaea mexicana''  Zucc. Calflora. Retrieved December 2, 2024, from https://www.calflora.org/app/taxon?crn=5875</ref> with stoloniferous,<ref name = "VicFlora" /><ref name = "Flora of North America" /> up to 30 cm long, and 4 cm wide rhizomes.<ref name = "VicFlora">Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria. (n.d.-b). ''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zucc. VicFlora Flora of Victoria. Retrieved December 2, 2024, from https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/fc0766f3-a2f3-432d-b997-48256d588310</ref> The rhizomes bear leaf and root scars.<ref name = "Zuccarini, 1832" /> The stolons are 15–100 cm long, and 0.5–1 cm wide.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The ovate, suborbicular,<ref name = "Zuccarini, 1832" /> or elliptic lamina is 7–18(–27) cm long, and 7–14(–18) cm wide.<ref name = "Flora of North America" /> The long, cylindrical petiole<ref name = "Zuccarini, 1832" /> is glabrous.<ref name = "Flora of North America" />

===Generative characteristics===
The  floating or emersed,<ref name = "Flora of North America" /> yellow, 6–13 cm wide flowers have peduncles with four primary air canals.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The flowers have four sepals<ref name = "Biota of New Zealand" /> and 12–30 yellow petals.<ref name = "Flora of North America" /> The [[androecium]] consists of 50 stamens.<ref name = "VicFlora" /> The [[gynoecium]] consists of seven to ten carpels.<ref name = "Flora of North America" /> The spheroid or ovoid fruit bears 3–5 mm long, and 3–5 mm wide seeds<ref name = "Flora of New Zealand">Manaaki Whenua – Landcare Research. (n.d.-c). ''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zucc. Flora of New Zealand. Retrieved December 3, 2024, from https://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/taxon/Nymphaea-mexicana.html</ref> with hairlike papillae.<ref name = "Flora of New Zealand" /><ref name = "Flora of North America" /> Tuberiferous flowers or proliferating [[pseudanthia]] can be present.<ref name = "Grob et al., 2006">{{cite journal|last1=Grob|first1=V.|last2=Moline|first2=P.|last3=Pfeifer|first3=E.|last4=Novelo|first4=A. R.|last5=Rutishauser|first5=R.|year=2006|title=Developmental morphology of branching flowers in ''Nymphaea prolifera''|journal=Journal of Plant Research|volume=119|issue=6|pages=561-570|pmid= 17021936|doi=10.1007/s10265-006-0021-8|url=https://www.zora.uzh.ch/server/api/core/bitstreams/fc8c59ed-16d6-4252-8571-ba6fed549430/content?trackerId=929068f5ac0f8435|access-date=5 October 2025|via=Zurich Open Repository and Archive}}</ref>

===Cytology===
The chromosome count is n = 28. The genome size is 586.80 Mb.<ref name = "Chen et al., 2017">{{cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Fei |last2=Liu |first2=Xing |last3=Yu |first3=Cuiwei |last4=Chen |first4=Yuchu |last5=Tang |first5=Haibao |last6=Zhang |first6=Liangsheng |title=Water lilies as emerging models for Darwin's abominable mystery |journal=Horticulture Research |date=2017 |volume=4 |issue=1 |page=17051 |doi=10.1038/hortres.2017.51 |pmid=28979789|doi-access=free |pmc=5626932 |bibcode=2017HorR....417051C }}</ref> The chloroplast genome is 159962 bp long.<ref name = "Gruenstaeudl et al., 2017">Gruenstaeudl, M., Nauheimer, L., & Borsch, T. (2017). [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318253682_Plastid_genome_structure_and_phylogenomics_of_Nymphaeales_conserved_gene_order_and_new_insights_into_relationships Plastid genome structure and phylogenomics of Nymphaeales: conserved gene order and new insights into relationships.] Plant systematics and evolution, 303, 1251-1270.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
It was published by [[Joseph Gerhard Zuccarini]] in 1832.<ref name = "Zuccarini, 1832">Königlich Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften. & Königlich Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften. (1832). Abhandlungen der Mathematisch-Physikalischen Klasse der Königlich Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften (Vol. 1, p. 365). https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/11355625</ref><ref name = "POWO, 2024 b" /> Within the subgenus [[Nymphaea subg. Nymphaea|''Nymphaea'' subg. ''Nymphaea'']]<ref name = "Pellicer et al., 2013">Pellicer, J., Kelly, L. J., Magdalena, C., & Leitch, I. J. (2013). [https://cdnsciencepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1139/gen-2013-0039 Insights into the dynamics of genome size and chromosome evolution in the early diverging angiosperm lineage Nymphaeales (water lilies).] Genome, 56(8), 437-449.</ref> it is placed in the section ''Nymphaea'' sect. ''Xanthantha''.<ref name = "Borsch et al., 2007">Borsch, T., Hilu, K. W., Wiersema, J. H., Löhne, C., Barthlott, W., & Wilde, V. (2007). [https://www.seerosenforum.de/Gattung/PHYLOGENY-OF-NYMPHAEA.pdf Phylogeny of ''Nymphaea'' (Nymphaeaceae): evidence from substitutions and microstructural changes in the chloroplast trnT-trnF region.] International Journal of Plant Sciences, 168(5), 639-671.</ref><ref name = "Conard, 1905">Conard,  Henry S. (1905). The waterlilies: a monograph of the genus ''Nymphaea'' (pp. 163–167). Pub. by the Carnegie Institution of Washington. https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/35044992</ref>

===Etymology===
The specific epithet ''mexicana'' refers to Mexico.<ref name = "Biota of New Zealand">Manaaki Whenua – Landcare Research. (n.d.-b). ''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zucc. Biota of New Zealand. Retrieved December 2, 2024, from https://biotanz.landcareresearch.co.nz/scientific-names/7170dae4-4e51-4868-be42-e5d9fa735353</ref>

===Hybridisation===
Together with ''[[Nymphaea odorata]]'', it forms the natural hybrid [[Nymphaea × thiona|''Nymphaea'' × ''thiona'']].<ref name = "Flora of North America" />

==Reproduction==
===Vegetative reproduction===
''Nymphaea mexicana'' reproduces vegetatively through stolons. Their structure, resembling bananas, consists of leaf buds and thick, starchy roots.<ref name = "Wiersema, 1988">Wiersema, J. H. (1988). Reproductive Biology of ''Nymphaea'' (Nymphaeaceae). Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden, 75(3), 795–804. https://doi.org/10.2307/2399367</ref> Additionally, tuberiferous flowers or proliferating pseudanthia can be present.<ref name = "Grob et al., 2006" />

==Conservation==
The [[NatureServe conservation status]] is Vulnerable (G3).<ref name = "NatureServe" />

==Ecology==
===Habitat===
It occurs in up to 4 m deep water<ref name = "Flora of Australia">S.W.L. Jacobs & C.L. Porter. ''Nymphaea mexicana'', in (ed.), Flora of Australia. Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water: Canberra. https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Nymphaea%20mexicana [Date Accessed: 04 December 2024]</ref> in lagoons, canals<ref name = "Alabama Plant Atlas" /> swamps, and rivers.<ref name = "Florabase">Western Australian Herbarium & Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions. (n.d.-c). ''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zucc. Florabase—the Western Australian Flora. Retrieved December 3, 2024, from https://florabase.dbca.wa.gov.au/browse/profile/2922</ref> It can occur in brackish water.<ref name = "Alabama Plant Atlas">Alabama Herbarium Consortium & University of West Alabama. (n.d.). ''Nymphaea mexicana''. Alabama Plant Atlas. Retrieved December 3, 2024, from http://floraofalabama.org/Plant.aspx?id=2705</ref>

===Herbivory===
The [[canvasback]] duck, ''Aythya valisineria'', feeds on the banana-like roots of the plant.<ref name="BirdsOfTheWorld-A-valisineria">{{cite web | last=Mowbray | first=Thomas B. | title=Canvasback (''Aythya valisineria'') | website=Birds of the World | publisher=[[Cornell Lab of Ornithology]] | date=2020-03-04 | url=http://birdsoftheworld.org/bow/species/canvas/cur/introduction | access-date=2021-04-20}}</ref>

===As an invasive species===
Together with its hybrids, it has become an invasive species outside of its natural range.<ref name = "Reid et al., 2023">Reid, M. K., Paterson, I. D., Coetzee, J. A., Gettys, L. A., & Hill, M. P. (2023). [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1049964423001445 Know thy enemy: Investigating genetic contributions from putative parents of invasive ''Nymphaea mexicana'' hybrids in South Africa as part of efforts to develop biological control.] Biological Control, 184, 105291.</ref><ref name = "Reid et al., 2021">Reid, M. K., Naidu, P., Paterson, I. D., Mangan, R., & Coetzee, J. A. (2021). [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/am/pii/S0304377021000218 Population genetics of invasive and native ''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zuccarini: Taking the first steps to initiate a biological control programme in South Africa.] Aquatic Botany, 171, 103372.</ref> For instance, it has been recorded in [[Australia]],<ref name = "VicFlora" /><ref name = "Florabase" /> [[South Africa]],<ref name = "Reid et al., 2023" /> [[New Zealand]],<ref name = "Flora of New Zealand" /><ref name = "Biota of New Zealand" /> and the [[Iberian Peninsula]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Martínez Bautista |first1=M.C. |last2=Guerra Barena |first2=M.J. |last3=Gutiérrez Esteban |first3=M. |title=Invasión de ''Nymphaea mexicana'' Zucc. (Nymphaceae) en la cuenca del río Guadiana |journal=Folia Bot. Extremadurensis |date=2012 |volume=6 |pages=39–44 |url=https://dialnet.unirioja.es/descarga/articulo/6425933.pdf}}</ref>
